content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Logical Replication and Publication/Subscription in PostgreSQL"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"PostgreSQL logical replication provides a robust mechanism for replicating data objects and their changes, based on their replication identity (usually a primary key). Unlike physical replication, which operates at the byte level of the entire cluster, logical replication allows selective replication of tables and finer-grained control over data routing."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Prerequisites and Configuration"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Before setting up publications and subscriptions, you must configure the PostgreSQL instance to allow logical replication. Open your postgresql.conf file and ensure the wal_level parameter is set to logical."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"wal_level = logical"},{"order":6,"type":"paragraph","text":"You will also need to restart the PostgreSQL service and ensure that max_replication_slots and max_wal_senders are set to values greater than zero."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"Creating a Publication on the Publisher"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"A publication is defined on a primary database, often referred to as the publisher. It represents a set of changes generated by a table or a group of tables. You can create a publication for all tables or specify individual tables."},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"CREATE PUBLICATION my_publication FOR TABLE users, orders;"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"If you want to publish all tables in the database automatically, you can use the following command:"},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"CREATE PUBLICATION all_tables_pub FOR ALL TABLES;"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Creating a Subscription on the Subscriber"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"The subscription is defined on the target database, known as the subscriber. The subscriber connects to the publisher and requests the data and incremental changes for the specified publication."},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"Ensure that the target tables already exist on the subscriber with a schema compatible with the publisher tables."},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"CREATE SUBSCRIPTION my_subscription CONNECTION 'host=publisher_host port=5432 dbname=mydb user=repl_user password=secret' PUBLICATION my_publication;"},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"Monitoring and Managing Replication"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"PostgreSQL provides built-in catalog views to monitor the health and status of logical replication. On the publisher side, you can track replication slots and connected subscribers."},{"order":18,"type":"code","text":"SELECT * FROM pg_replication_slots;"},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"On the subscriber side, you can check the status of the subscription workers using the subscriber catalog view."},{"order":20,"type":"code","text":"SELECT * FROM pg_stat_subscription;"},{"order":21,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices and Limitations"},{"order":22,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Tables must have a primary key or a replica identity set to ensure row updates and deletions can be applied correctly on the subscriber."},{"order":23,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Logical replication does not replicate schema changes (DDL). Any table alterations must be applied manually to both the publisher and subscriber."},{"order":24,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Truncate operations are supported, but must be configured carefully with the appropriate cascading options on the publisher."}]
